name: Daphne Mills
life: “I still remember a brother who used to follow his own shadow.” On Monday, near Paper & Pine Books, Daphne starts with the handwritten shelf cards and often leaves with a suggestion for somebody else.
voice: The shadow makes her look like my brother at four. I bring my dad down at that exact hour.
appearance: On an ordinary day, look for a gray fisher's sweater and a train token tied to a zipper pull. Daphne has a softly rounded chin under sharp cheekbones, with a loose dark braid. Daphne starts to lift a hand, then waits to be invited to speak during a conversation.
personality: Is a careful borrower and a reckless lender. Things leave this person's house with elaborate instructions and very little expectation of ever coming back.
agenda: To bring the father at the hour of the familiar shadow.
family: Nadia Carvalho is Daphne’s cousin. Daphne calls about good news first. Nadia is allowed to ask about the bad news afterward. Neither wants every family conversation to begin with a bill, a diagnosis or an apology. Asked about *A widow bids again*, Nadia says, “I was asked to testify the building was sound.”
connections: Anthony Bell. Two angles fit on a postcard that the father can revisit.
